Two legacy paths share this message. The auth-request login flow's user lookup re-applies any events newer than its cached view before answering, and only returns this when the user has no view row and no events at all (unknown ID) or the freshly-applied events show the user was deleted; GetHumanOTPSecret returns it when an OTP configuration exists but never reached the ready state, which the API then treats as if no OTP were configured.

Generic fallback used across dozens of unrelated code paths — an unhandled branch in the legacy login-flow state machine, a failed JSON unmarshal of stored event data, a panic from a SQL query-builder call, and similar defensive should-not-happen checks. There is no single trigger for this cluster; each call site guards a different unexpected server-side fault rather than something the caller did wrong.

Loading the org's domain/username policy (falling back to the instance default) failed while validating a username change or user removal — this wraps whatever underlying lookup error occurred, rather than pointing at one specific missing setting.
